nachricht_auszug: The Sophos AP15 seems to be very close to Sophos AP55/AP100.
Unique to AP15: Green and yellow LED; 2T2R 2.4GHz 802.11b/g/n via SoC WMAC; No buttons; No piezo beeper; No 5.8GHz

Flashing: TFTP server 192.168.99.8/24, initramfs as e.g. boot.bin; open AP's enclosure and locate UART header (there is a video online); 115200 8/N/1; cancel autoboot, prompt 'ath> '; tftpboot 0x81000000 boot.bin; bootm 0x81000000; then IP 192.168.1.1/24, flash sysupgrade via web ui
(BTW: the AP55 images seem to work too, only LEDs are not working)
Testing: flashed onto two devices, MAC addresses are correct, LEDs are working, scanning for WLANs is working

openwrt_git_ohne_5ghz.nachricht: Sophos AP15 only uses the SoC's built-in wifi. There's no external PCIe chipset.

openwrt_git_qca9557.nachricht: the AP15 uses a QCA9557 SoC (which only has two chains enabled in the package or silicon). This is mostly cosmetic since QCA9558 and QCA9557 are virtually identical

nachricht_auszug: The Sophos AP15C uses the same hardware as the AP15, but has a reset button.
Unique to AP15C: Reset button; External RJ45 serial console port
Flash via Sophos SG/XG appliance (awetool, mtd -r write /tmp/openwrt.bin astaro_image) or U-Boot: TFTP 192.168.99.8/24, file 'uImage_AP15C', tftpboot; cp.b $fileaddr 0x9f070000 $filesize; boot

Specifications common to all models (AP100/AP100C/AP55/AP55C): QCA9558 @ 720 MHz, 128 MB RAM, 16 MB SPI flash, 1x 10/100/1000 Ethernet 802.3af PoE-in, Serial UART header on PCB, Alternate power supply via 5.5x2.1mm DC jack @ 12 VDC

[4] On AP100/AP55 models the UART header is accessible after removing the device's top cover. On AP100C/AP55C models, the PCB must be removed for access; three screws secure it to the case. Pin 1 is marked on the silkscreen. Pins from 1-4 are 3.3V, GND, TX, RX
